answer: Structural normative model repository (~58k subjects; cortical thickness, subcortical volume, surface area)
Functional normative model multi-site dataset (~21,474 controls across 40 sites; includes ABCD, CAMCAN, CMI-HBN, HCP Aging/Development/Early Psychosis/Young Adult, NKI-RS, PNC, UKBiobank)
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Structural models rely on a pre-trained repository (~58k). Functional models are trained/tested on a 40-site resting-state cohort (~21,474 controls) and transferred to OpenNeuro ds000243/ds002843/ds003798. Benchmarking tasks draw on HCP (cognition regression) plus COBRE and UMich schizophrenia samples (group difference/classification).
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "For the structural data, we used a publicly shared repository of pre- trained normative models that were estimated on approximately 58,000 subjects..."; "Data from 40 sites were combined to create the initial full sample... including ABCD... CAMCAN... CMI-HBN... HCP-Aging... HCP-Development... HCP-Early Psychosis... HCP-Young Adult... NKI-RS... PNC... and UKBiobank..."; "we leveraged three datasets (ds000243, ds002843, ds003798) from OpenNeuro.org to create a multi-site transfer dataset."; "Datasets included the Human Connectome Project (young adult) study, the University of Michigan schizophrenia study, and the Center for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) schizophrenia study."

answer.Structural normative repository: Normative training source for cortical thickness, subcortical volume, and surface area models
answer.Functional multi-site dataset (~21,474 c: Normative training/testing set (80/20 split) for functional connectivity models
answer.OpenNeuro ds000243/ds002843/ds003798: Transfer/validation datasets for functional models at unseen sites
answer.HCP Young Adult: Used in functional model training/testing and as regression benchmark dataset (predicting cognition)
answer.COBRE: Benchmark dataset for schizophrenia vs control classification and group difference testing; transferred functional/structural models
answer.UMich SchizGaze: Benchmark dataset for schizophrenia vs control classification and group difference testing; transferred functional/structural models

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Functional models trained and tested on multi-site controls (with HCP YA contributing); OpenNeuro sites evaluate transfer. Structural repository supplies pre-trained models applied to benchmarking datasets. COBRE and UMich provide patient/control cohorts for group difference and SVM classification; HCP YA supports regression task.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Training and testing datasets (80/20) were created using scikit-learn's train_test_split function, stratifying on the site variable... three datasets (ds000243, ds002843, ds003798) from OpenNeuro.org to create a multi-site transfer dataset."; "The HCP data was used in the prediction - regression benchmarking task. The COBRE and UMich datasets are used in the classification and group difference testing benchmarking tasks."; "evaluation of the functional normative models was performed in a test set (20% of the training set) and in two transfer sets that are comprised of scanning sites not seen by the model during training (clinical and healthy controls)."

dc3_number_of_healthy_control.detail: Functional cohort totals computed by summing per-site train/test Ns in Supplementary file 1 (train 14,376; test 7,098; overall 21,474 controls). Structural repository reported as ~58,000 subjects used to estimate pre-trained models; treated as both overall and training size.

dc4_age_info.detail: Functional means/SDs computed as weighted mean and pooled SD across per-site train/test age (m, s.d.) values in Supplementary file 1. Median/IQR/min/max not reported. Structural repository described as spanning ages 2–100 with no summary statistics; min/max recorded, other fields NR.
